ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontally placed rectangle, and another rectangle congruent to it is placed tilted. The shaded part is the overlapping region of the two, forming a parallelogram. The lower-left corner and upper-right corner of the horizontal rectangle also respectively lie on one diagonal of the tilted rectangle, so they can be regarded as the endpoints of one diagonal shared by the two rectangles. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let the lower-left corner of the horizontal rectangle be A=(0,0), and the upper-right corner be C=(9,3). The tilted rectangle is congruent to the horizontal rectangle, with side lengths 9 and 3, and A and C are endpoints of one diagonal of the tilted rectangle. Let one long-side vector of the tilted rectangle be u=(x,y), with length 9; the other short-side vector be v=(9-x,3-y), with length 3. Because u+v=(9,3), and u is perpendicular to v, therefore u·(u+v)=u·(9,3)=|u|^2=81. Thus 9x+3y=81, that is, 3x+y=27. Also because |u|=9, x^2+y^2=81. Combining y=27-3x gives x^2+(27-3x)^2=81, solving gives the non-horizontal case u=(7.2,5.4). Therefore the slope of the long side is 5.4/7.2=3/4. The corresponding short-side vector is v=(1.8,-2.4). In the horizontal rectangle 0≤y≤3, the overlapping region formed by the two tilted long sides and the horizontal sides is a parallelogram. The overlap lengths on the upper and lower horizontal sides are both 5 cm, and the vertical height is 3 cm, so the area is 5×3=15 cm².

raw_record.question_text: Two identical rectangles with sides of length $3 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $9 \mathrm{~cm}$ are overlapping as in the diagram. What is the area of the overlap of the two rectangles?

method.method_draft: Coordinate/vector route. From the diagram, take the horizontal rectangle as having bottom-left corner A=(0,0), top-right corner C=(9,3), so the two rectangles share the diagonal AC. The slanted rectangle is the other 3-by-9 rectangle with A and C as opposite vertices. Let one side vector of the slanted rectangle be u=(x,y) with length 9, and the other be v=(9-x,3-y) with length 3, perpendicular to u. Since u+v=(9,3) and |u|=9, use u·(9,3)=|u|^2=81, giving 9x+3y=81, or 3x+y=27, together with x^2+y^2=81. The non-horizontal solution is u=(7.2,5.4), v=(1.8,-2.4). Thus the slanted long edges have slope 5.4/7.2=3/4. In the horizontal rectangle, these two slanted edges intersect the bottom/top horizontal sides so that the overlap is a parallelogram of vertical height 3 and horizontal base 5. Therefore the overlap area is 5·3=15 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Angle/similarity route. From the diagram, observe that both rectangles share the same diagonal from the lower-left corner of the horizontal rectangle to the upper-right corner. In a 3-by-9 rectangle, the diagonal makes an angle α with the long side satisfying tan α=3/9=1/3. The tilted rectangle lies on the other side of this common diagonal, so its long side makes angle 2α with the horizontal long side of the fixed rectangle. Hence the slope of the tilted long sides is tan(2α)=2(1/3)/(1-(1/3)^2)=3/4. A line of slope 3/4 rises 3 cm over a horizontal run of 4 cm. Therefore, along the 9 cm top edge of the horizontal rectangle, the part before the slanted side enters the overlap is 4 cm, leaving an overlap base of 9-4=5 cm. The overlap is a parallelogram with height 3 cm and base 5 cm, so its area is 15 cm^2.
